hook: Free storage on my wall beat a $2,000 slatwall quote

scenes.visual_prompt: Crowded garage floor with a car, bike, lawn mower, and stacked bins fighting for space
scenes.voiceover: My garage floor is basically a parking negotiation.

scenes.visual_prompt: Camera pans up to reveal completely bare wall space above 4 feet
scenes.voiceover: This whole strip has been empty the entire time.

scenes.visual_prompt: Split-screen graphic comparing a $2,000 slatwall installation quote against a $15.99 floating shelf price tag
scenes.voiceover: I compared both — the shelf route wins on cost per square foot.

scenes.visual_prompt: Mounting floating shelves with a stud finder and drill
Loading the shelf with heavy paint cans and tool bags, no sagging visible
scenes.voiceover: That's the actual failure point of cheap shelving — this one doesn't have it.

scenes.visual_prompt: Wide shot of three shelf tiers mounted at different heights, fully loaded
scenes.on_screen_text: Vertical storage, visible at a glance.
scenes.voiceover: This is what a showroom wall looks like instead of a dumping ground.

scenes.visual_prompt: Text card over the finished wall

caption: I almost paid $2,000 for a slatwall install before doing the math on floating shelves instead — $15.99 for 3, 4.5 stars, holds real weight. Full $91 garage system on the blog.
